Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How mass is calculated

Find mass from density and volume using m = ρV, with matching unit choices and equivalent outputs in grams and kilograms. The estimate assumes density is uniform throughout the object and that the chosen density matches its material and conditions. A 2 L volume of water at about 1 kg/L has a mass near 2 kg. The calculation validates each input and keeps its stated units explicit. Mass is intrinsic; apparent weight changes with gravity. This is an estimate for the stated assumptions; confirm measurements and any applicable professional or local standards before relying on it.

mass = density × volume
A worked example

A 2 L volume of water at about 1 kg/L has a mass near 2 kg.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

Does mass change with location?

Mass is intrinsic; apparent weight changes with gravity.

What if an object has mixed materials?

Calculate each part separately and add the masses, or use a measured average density.
